CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. If the skin of a drum is loose, the sound is (1 mark)
   A. louder than a tight skin always
   B. the same as a tight skin
   C. higher
   D. lower

2. How should a good netball player treat the other team at the end? (1 mark)
   A. Shout at them
   B. Ignore them
   C. Shake hands and thank them
   D. Tease them

3. When is an overhead pass most useful? (1 mark)
   A. When shooting from far
   B. When you are alone on the court
   C. When a defender is standing close
   D. When resting

4. How high is the goal ring above the ground? (1 mark)
   A. 3.05 metres
   B. 10 metres
   C. 5 metres
   D. 1.5 metres

5. What is the main reason for improvising a netball? (1 mark)
   A. Because real balls are always bad
   B. To avoid playing
   C. To use available materials when balls are not enough
   D. To spend more money

6. Which colours are the primary colours? (1 mark)
   A. Orange, green and purple
   B. Red, yellow and blue
   C. Black, white and grey
   D. Red, green and brown

7. A darker tone of a colour is called a (1 mark)
   A. tint
   B. secondary
   C. frame
   D. shade

8. What is a palette? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of brush
   B. A frame
   C. A type of paper
   D. A surface for mixing paint

9. Blue mixed with red makes (1 mark)
   A. yellow
   B. green
   C. purple
   D. orange

10. On the colour wheel, orange sits between (1 mark)
   A. yellow and blue
   B. red and yellow
   C. red and blue
   D. blue and green

11. How many beats does each bar have in the four-beat patterns of this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Six
   B. Two
   C. Eight
   D. Four

12. A monotone line in music writing is (1 mark)
   A. a colour
   B. a very loud note
   C. a single line on which notes are written
   D. a five-line staff

13. Listening for the name of a note without seeing it is called (1 mark)
   A. painting
   B. drawing
   C. aural work
   D. running

14. How far apart are the hands placed at the start? (1 mark)
   A. One on each side of the track
   B. As far as possible
   C. Touching each other
   D. Shoulder-width apart

15. The shield and two crossed spears on the flag stand for (1 mark)
   A. farming
   B. sports
   C. music
   D. defence of freedom

16. How does gymnastics help the heart and lungs? (1 mark)
   A. Moving the whole body makes the heart beat faster and stay strong
   B. It has no effect
   C. It stops the heart
   D. It removes the lungs

17. Which health benefit comes from gymnastics? (1 mark)
   A. Less energy
   B. Better flexibility
   C. Weaker bones
   D. Slower breathing always

18. Which is a way to give good feedback to a partner? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh at their mistakes
   B. Push them
   C. Say one thing that was good and one thing to improve
   D. Say nothing

19. Which is a safe surface for gymnastics? (1 mark)
   A. Concrete
   B. A mat or soft clean ground
   C. A stony floor
   D. Wet tiles

20. Unison singing is suitable for an anthem because (1 mark)
   A. it is silent
   B. everyone can join in the same tune
   C. it uses no notes
   D. it needs instruments

21. Why use a camera strap? (1 mark)
   A. To keep it wet
   B. To cover the lens
   C. So the camera does not drop
   D. To make it heavy

22. What should you do before photographing someone? (1 mark)
   A. Take it secretly
   B. Take photos of strangers only
   C. Shout at them
   D. Ask their permission

23. Why delete poor photographs? (1 mark)
   A. To make the screen dark
   B. To break the camera
   C. To cool it
   D. So memory is not filled up

24. On the staff, the note B sits on (1 mark)
   A. line 2
   B. line 3
   C. line 5
   D. line 1

25. When you make a mistake while playing in a group, you should (1 mark)
   A. throw your recorder
   B. shout
   C. carry on with the beat
   D. stop the whole group

26. The top part of the recorder is the (1 mark)
   A. middle joint
   B. bell
   C. head joint
   D. foot joint

27. Which is a safe way to enter the pool? (1 mark)
   A. Jumping onto others
   B. Feet first, watched by the teacher
   C. Being pushed
   D. Head first from a run

28. Which game builds strong arms and shoulders as you crawl on hands and toes? (1 mark)
   A. Crocodile crawl
   B. Snake slither
   C. Giraffe stretch
   D. Elephant walk

29. Which material can you use to make a portfolio? (1 mark)
   A. Iron sheets
   B. Sand
   C. Glass
   D. Manila paper or cardboard

30. What is used to close a homemade portfolio? (1 mark)
   A. A string or ribbon tie
   B. A padlock
   C. Nails
   D. Wet glue only

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain the difference between a sacred song and a patriotic song. (3 marks)

32. State two ways of playing percussion instruments. (2 marks)

33. Explain how to make a tint of blue. (2 marks)

34. State four things you would look for when appreciating a sports performance. (4 marks)

35. What is the centre of interest in a photograph? (3 marks)

36. Explain how to perform an animal game to a musical rhythm. (4 marks)

37. State three qualities of good feedback. (3 marks)

38. Give four steps of a double-handed catch. (4 marks)

39. Why should we enter the water feet first? (2 marks)

40. Why should the flag stick be held high while cheering? (2 marks)

41. State two ways to keep the working area clean after painting. (2 marks)

42. Why should you never point a camera directly at the sun? (3 marks)

43. Describe how to do the elephant walk. (3 marks)

44. Give three ways of caring for a digital camera. (3 marks)

45. Describe a full netball court. (3 marks)

46. What does giving with the ball mean in netball catching? (2 marks)

47. What does singing in unison mean? Why is it good for an anthem? (3 marks)

48. State the three commands at the start of a sprint race in order. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — lower
   A loose skin vibrates more slowly, so the sound is lower.

2. C — Shake hands and thank them
   Fair play means being respectful whether you win or lose.

3. C — When a defender is standing close
   The ball goes over the defender's arms.

4. A — 3.05 metres
   The netball goal ring is 3.05 metres high.

5. C — To use available materials when balls are not enough
   Improvising lets us practise with materials we already have.

6. B — Red, yellow and blue
   Primary colours cannot be made by mixing other colours.

7. D — shade
   Adding black makes a shade.

8. D — A surface for mixing paint
   A palette is where paints are mixed.

9. C — purple
   Blue and red give purple.

10. B — red and yellow
   Orange is made from red and yellow, so it sits between them.

11. D — Four
   The patterns of this lesson have four beats.

12. C — a single line on which notes are written
   On a monotone we write the rhythm on one line.

13. C — aural work
   Aural work uses the ears to identify notes.

14. D — Shoulder-width apart
   Hands are about shoulder-width apart.

15. D — defence of freedom
   The shield and spears represent the defence of freedom.

16. A — Moving the whole body makes the heart beat faster and stay strong
   Active movement strengthens the heart and lungs.

17. B — Better flexibility
   Stretching and rolling help joints and muscles bend freely.

18. C — Say one thing that was good and one thing to improve
   Kind and helpful feedback includes praise and a suggestion.

19. B — A mat or soft clean ground
   Soft, flat surfaces prevent injuries.

20. B — everyone can join in the same tune
   A single tune that everybody sings is simple and strong.

21. C — So the camera does not drop
   A strap protects the device from falls.

22. D — Ask their permission
   Permission is polite and safe.

23. D — So memory is not filled up
   Deleting saves space.

24. B — line 3
   B is on the middle line.

25. C — carry on with the beat
   Continue and rejoin.

26. C — head joint
   The head joint has the mouthpiece.

27. B — Feet first, watched by the teacher
   Feet-first entry is safe.

28. A — Crocodile crawl
   Body held straight on hands and toes.

29. D — Manila paper or cardboard
   Manila paper folds easily.

30. A — A string or ribbon tie
   Punched holes with string keep it closed.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: A sacred song is a song of worship that praises God. A patriotic song shows love for the country, such as the national anthem.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning, 1 mark for an example.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: Striking and shaking. Scraping is also correct.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: Add white to blue, a little at a time, until it is as light as you want.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for white, 1 mark for adding gradually.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Teamwork, skill, safety and sportsmanship.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: The main subject that you want the viewer to notice first, for example a friend's face or a flower.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for main subject, 1 mark for noticed first, 1 mark for an example.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a game and a rhythm, clap or drum the beat, move to the beat, change the speed for different animals and add a song.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Kind, honest, specific and helpful. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: Watch the ball into your hands; reach out with both hands; spread the fingers with the thumbs close; bend the arms and pull the ball to the chest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is safer because you cannot hit your head on the bottom, and you can see where you land.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: So it does not hit other people, and so the flag can be seen.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Wash the brushes and containers, wipe the desk, put the paper in the bin. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: It can hurt your eyes and the strong light will spoil the picture.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for eyes, 1 mark for picture, 1 mark for explanation.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Bend forward at the waist, clasp hands so that the arms hang like a trunk, and walk slowly with heavy steps, swaying the trunk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hold with two hands; use a strap; clean the lens with a soft dry cloth; keep away from water and dust; charge the battery. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is a rectangle 30.5 metres long and 15.25 metres wide. It is divided into three equal thirds. It has a goal post at each end with a goal circle and a centre circle in the middle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rectangle with measurements, 1 mark for thirds, 1 mark for circles or posts.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Bending the arms as the ball arrives so as to take the force out of it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for bending arms, 1 mark for softening the catch.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Everyone sings the same notes at the same time. It is simple and everybody can join in together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 2 marks for the reason.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: On your marks, set, go.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for all three, 1 mark for the correct order.
